headline: First edition of the migration tab. Pressure from Belarus is concentrated on Latvia, where attempted illegal crossings in 2026 already exceed the whole of 2025, and Latvia wants to keep its special border regime until mid-2027. On the EU side, the Baltic states are formally classed as at risk and cannot be made to accept relocated migrants; no transfers of migrants to the Baltic states from other EU countries have been reported.
pressure_note: Latvia's border guard says 12,857 people were stopped trying to cross from Belarus by 10 November, above the 12,046 for all of 2025; recent daily figures are in the tens. Smugglers, tunnels and damage to border equipment continue. Lithuania and Poland see far fewer attempts, and Estonia closes its road crossings with Russia on 1 December.
eu_note: Under the EU Migration Pact each country chooses whether to take people, pay or send other support; Latvia and Lithuania say they will not take relocated migrants, and Estonia may ask to have its share reduced. The 2027 round is being negotiated after the Commission's 6 November report. Germany is resuming returns under EU rules to Italy and Greece, not the Baltic states.
changed: First edition, so there is no earlier day to compare with. Counts cover items reported between 10 and 17 November; from tomorrow they cover only what is new since the previous edition.
bottom_line: The evidence points to two different kinds of risk. The immediate one is pressure organised from Belarus: Latvian prosecutors describe smuggling networks, payments of about 5,000 dollars a crossing, migrants pushed to damage border equipment and suspected involvement of Belarusian border officials, which fits the hybrid pressure described in Lithuania's 2026 threat assessment. The second, which many people fear, is that other EU countries will shift their migrants onto the Baltic states. Under current rules that is limited: relocation is voluntary in practice, fewer than 1,000 people are expected to be physically relocated across the whole EU in 2026, and the Baltic states have declined to take any. The lawful channel that could grow is returns of people who first entered the EU through Latvia or Lithuania and moved on west; Poland already checks its border with Lithuania until March 2027 and turns people back. Claims that the EU forces the Baltic states to take thousands of migrants are not supported by the rules or the numbers. Daily crossing numbers swing widely and are published unevenly, so single days say little.

headline: Lithuania moves to take no relocated migrants under the EU solidarity scheme and pay instead, replacing a May pledge to take 58 from Cyprus; in Estonia, parties argue over checks on the Latvian border. No new organised crossing incidents or transfers of migrants to the Baltic states were reported.
pressure_note: No new daily crossing figures were found since the previous edition. The latest: Latvia stopped 12,857 attempts by 10 November; Lithuania turned back 1,896 people by 7 November, already more than the 1,652 in all of 2025; Poland recorded 482 attempts by 8 November and plans to extend its Belarus border buffer zone to 27 February 2027, citing drones and balloons. Belarus also ordered a snap readiness check of its border-guard units.
eu_note: A Lithuanian government commission approved the interior minister's proposal to take no relocated migrants and pay into the EU solidarity pool instead; the government still has to approve it and the amount is not yet known. The Pact allows this choice. Five EU states announced a Rwanda return hub for rejected asylum seekers, which Estonia supports but will not join; it does not change Baltic obligations. No transfers to the Baltic states were reported.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30, with no rating changes; trends move from New to Unchanged. All five counts are 0 (yesterday: organised incidents 1, new border measures 2, misleading claims 2). New since yesterday: Lithuania's plan to pay instead of relocating anyone; the Estonian party debate on checks at the Latvian border; the Rwanda return hub. Catching up: Poland's draft to extend its Belarus buffer zone (14 November) and Lithuania's year-to-date figure. Correction: yesterday's edition said the Baltic states have declined to take any relocated migrants; in fact Lithuania agreed in May to take 58 from Cyprus, a choice it is now moving to replace with a payment.
bottom_line: Today's news mostly concerns how the Baltic states use the choices the EU rules give them, not anything imposed on them. Lithuania's move to pay rather than relocate shows that the solidarity scheme lets a country refuse relocation entirely, which again contradicts claims that the EU forces the Baltic states to take migrants; it also shows that Lithuania had earlier volunteered to take a small group, so the picture is a national choice, not a refusal from the start. The organised pressure from Belarus continues on the evidence of recent weeks, with Latvia most affected and Lithuania's own turn-backs now above last year's total, although no fresh daily figures were published in this window. The Estonian debate on checks at the Latvian border is about onward movement inside Schengen and is partly driven by opposition parties; the government is not proposing checks. No other EU country has been reported planning to send migrants to the Baltic states; lawful returns between EU states remain a separate and, for now, quiet channel.

headline: Lithuania's interior minister rejects accusations of xenophobia over his plan to pay into the EU solidarity pool instead of taking relocated migrants, saying it is cheaper. Lithuania recorded no crossing attempts from Belarus for three days while Latvia stopped 88 in four days; Estonia puts the cost of checks on the Latvian border at €65 million and sees no need for them now.
pressure_note: New figures: Lithuania recorded no attempts to cross from Belarus outside official crossing points on 15–17 November after turning back seven people on 14 November, bringing its 2026 total to 1,962 against 1,652 in all of 2025. Latvia stopped 12, 41, 29 and 6 attempts on 14–17 November. The pressure remains concentrated on Latvia. Figures count attempts, not people, and are published unevenly.
eu_note: No EU decision, transfer or plan to send migrants to the Baltic states was reported. Lithuania's interior minister repeated that the country will pay into the solidarity pool next year rather than accept relocated people, and said the decision is political and financial; the amount is not yet set. This is a choice the Pact allows. Poland and Estonia are exempt from contributing.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30, with no rating changes, and all five counts stay at 0. New since yesterday: fresh border figures from Lithuania (three days with no attempts, 1,962 so far this year) and Latvia (88 attempts on 14–17 November); Lithuania's interior minister rejected xenophobia accusations and said paying is cheaper than relocation over five years; Estonia's interior ministry put the cost of Latvian border checks at about €65 million and said they are not needed now; Estonia's parliament advanced the bill to close crossings with Russia. Catching up: an Estonian court report (16 November) on a plea-bargain conviction for driving five migrants from Latvia into Estonia.
bottom_line: Organised pressure from Belarus continues but is uneven: Latvia still stops dozens of attempts most days, while Lithuania has had a quiet spell, and day-to-day swings in these figures should not be read as a trend because they count attempts and are published irregularly. The EU side is quiet: no other EU state has been reported planning to send migrants to the Baltic states, and Lithuania's decision to pay rather than relocate again shows the solidarity scheme does not force anyone to take people. The minister's cost argument is plausible but unproven, since no figures have been published and the payment amount is not set. In Estonia, the government's own estimate and its statement that checks on the Latvian border are not needed now undercut opposition claims that onward migration through Latvia requires them, though the €65 million figure differs from earlier numbers in the debate. Lawful returns between EU states and pressure organised from Belarus remain separate issues, and only the second is active this week.

headline: Latvia's tally of prevented crossings from Belarus has passed 13,000 this year, above all of 2025 and nearing the 2023 record. Lithuania drafts a fence plan for parts of its Kaliningrad border. No EU decision or transfer that would send migrants to the Baltic states was reported.
pressure_note: No new daily border figures were published after 17 November in the sources found. Latvia's running total reached about 13,012 prevented attempts by 16 November (plus 6 on 17 November), against 12,046 in all of 2025 and a record 13,863 in 2023; border guards note the figures can count the same person several times. Lithuania recorded no attempts on 15–17 November and 1,962 so far this year. Pressure remains concentrated on Latvia.
eu_note: No new EU decision, transfer or plan to send migrants to the Baltic states. Under the Commission's 6 November assessment, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia are 'at risk' (priority access to EU support), and Estonia is also among six states facing a significant situation that may ask for reductions in their solidarity contributions. The Council is expected to set the 2027 solidarity pool before the end of the year.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30, with no rating changes, and all five counts stay at 0. New since yesterday: Lithuania's border guard service presented a plan to fence parts of the Kaliningrad border, which still needs funding; a correction to our earlier wording, that Poland and Estonia are 'exempt' from the solidarity pool: the Commission lists them among states that may request deductions, which is not yet an exemption for 2027; Lithuania cut its 2027 quota for foreign workers to 24,400, a labour-migration matter separate from asylum. Catching up: Latvia's 2026 total passed 13,000 on 16 November, and Estonian police say over 400 people caught in Estonia this year were returned to Latvia under a bilateral arrangement.
bottom_line: Organised pressure from Belarus continues, and Latvia's year total now exceeds all of 2025, which supports the Elevated rating; but the totals count attempts, the same person may be counted several times, and no new daily figures appeared in the last two days, so no short-term trend can be drawn. On the EU side nothing new points to other states shifting migrants onto the Baltic states: the Commission's designations give all three priority access to support, and the main open question is the 2027 pool the Council still has to set. The only regular transfers involving the Baltic states found this week are lawful returns from Estonia to Latvia of people who moved north after crossing from Belarus, which is a consequence of the Belarus route, not a burden shifted from western Europe. Lithuania's Kaliningrad fence plan is aimed mainly at hybrid threats and possible Russian draft evaders, not at a current migration flow. Coverage that treats Lithuania's or Estonia's pool status as settled runs ahead of the decision, which has not been taken.

headline: A quiet day on the migration front: no new border-guard figures were published after 17 November, and no EU decision or transfer that would send migrants to the Baltic states was reported. Estonia formally approves closing its road crossings with Russia from 1 December. A check of earlier figures finds Estonia's returns to Latvia were overstated in our 20 November edition.
pressure_note: No new daily figures found after 17 November. Latvia's 2026 total stood at about 13,012 prevented attempts on 16 November, above the 12,046 of all 2025; border guards note that the same person may be counted several times. Lithuania recorded no attempts on 15–17 November and about 1,962 this year. Pressure remains concentrated on Latvia.
eu_note: No new EU decision, transfer or plan to send migrants to the Baltic states. Under the Commission's 6 November assessment Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia are 'at risk', which gives them priority access to EU support, and Estonia may request deductions from its solidarity contribution. The Council is still expected to set the 2027 solidarity pool before the end of the year.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30, with no rating changes, and all five counts stay at 0. New since yesterday: Estonia's government formally approved closing all five road crossings with Russia from 1 December (the decision was counted on 17 November); Moscow says it will respond politically and diplomatically. Correction: an ERR report of 3 November said 148 of 388 migrants found in Estonia this year had been handed back to Latvia, so yesterday's figure of 'over 400 returned' appears to confuse people caught with people returned.
bottom_line: With no fresh border data since 17 November, the Elevated rating rests on Latvia's year total, which already exceeds 2025 but counts attempts rather than people; the gap in published figures means no trend can be read into the last few days. Nothing new suggests other EU states are shifting migrants onto the Baltic states; the only regular transfers found are lawful returns from Estonia to Latvia of people who entered via Belarus, and on the best available figure these number about 150 this year, not over 400. Estonia's border closure is driven by sabotage concerns, and its interior ministry's warning that Russia might push migrants toward the border afterwards is a contingency, not an observed movement. The open EU question remains the 2027 solidarity pool, which the Council has not yet set. Coverage that presents the Baltic states as facing compulsory relocation still runs ahead of the rules.

headline: Another quiet day at the borders: Latvia stopped 3 crossing attempts on 18 November, the latest figure published, bringing its year total to about 13,021. EU officials met on 20 November to examine the 2027 solidarity pool, with no decision yet. A recheck of Estonian figures suggests yesterday's correction on returns to Latvia went too far.
pressure_note: Latvia's border guard reported 3 prevented attempts on 18 November and about 13,021 this year, above the 12,046 of all 2025; the same person may be counted several times. No later daily figures were found. Lithuania's latest figures show no or few attempts in mid-November and about 1,962 this year. Pressure remains concentrated on Latvia.
eu_note: The EU's High-Level Solidarity Forum met in Brussels on 20 November to examine the proposed 2027 solidarity pool and a draft decision letting states under heavy migratory pressure reduce their contributions; the texts are restricted and no outcome has been published. No transfer or plan to send migrants to the Baltic states from western Europe was reported.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30, with no rating changes, and all five counts stay at 0. New since yesterday: Latvia's figure for 18 November (3 attempts; about 13,021 this year); the EU High-Level Solidarity Forum examined the 2027 pool on 20 November, a step before any Council decision. Correction to our 21 November edition: ERR's later report of 16 November says over 400 migrants caught in Estonia this year are then returned to Latvia, so yesterday's conclusion that only about 150 had been returned was too firm; the two ERR figures are now treated as conflicting.
bottom_line: With only one new daily figure since 17 November, the Elevated rating still rests on Latvia's year total, which already exceeds 2025 but counts attempts rather than people; no trend can be read from a few sparse days. The EU process is moving on schedule but behind closed doors: the 20 November forum examined the 2027 pool and possible deductions, and the Baltic states, rated 'at risk', stand to receive priority support rather than new obligations. The only regular movement of migrants into a Baltic state from another EU country remains Estonia's lawful returns to Latvia of people who arrived via Belarus; this is a knock-on effect of Belarus's route, not other EU states shifting their caseload onto the Baltics. How many have been returned is unclear: ERR reported 148 in early November and later implied more than 400, and we corrected ourselves too quickly yesterday. Estonia's road-crossing closure on 1 December is a security measure; a migrant push from Russia afterwards remains a contingency, not an observed movement.

headline: The European Court of Human Rights will rule tomorrow, 24 November, on pushbacks at the Belarus border by Poland, Latvia and Lithuania. No new daily crossing figures have been published since 18 November. Correction: Finland's parliament already extended its border asylum-restriction law to the end of 2028 on 18 November.
pressure_note: No new official daily figures were found after Latvia's 3 attempts on 18 November; Latvia's 2026 total is about 13,000 prevented attempts, above the 12,046 of all 2025, with repeat attempts by the same people counted each time. Lithuania's latest figures (about 1,962 this year) show few or no attempts in mid-November. Pressure remains concentrated on Latvia.
eu_note: The Council is expected to adopt the 2027 solidarity pool before the end of the year; no date or outcome has been published since the 20 November forum. Lithuania and Latvia are listed as 'at risk' (priority access to EU support), and Estonia also as facing a significant migratory situation, which lets it ask for reduced contributions. No transfer or plan to send migrants to the Baltic states from western Europe was reported.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30 with no status changes; the 'Pushback law, courts and rights' trend moves from Unchanged to Rising because the Grand Chamber ruling is now scheduled for 24 November. All five counts stay at 0. Correction to earlier editions, which said Finland's law was 'due to be extended': parliament approved the extension to the end of 2028 on 18 November, 170 votes to 19.
bottom_line: The most important migration event this week is legal, not at the border: tomorrow's Grand Chamber rulings in three cases from 2021–2022 will set out how far Poland, Latvia and Lithuania may turn people back at a border that Belarus uses for pressure, and both governments and rights groups will read them closely. Until then the Elevated pressure rating rests on Latvia's year total, which counts attempts rather than people, and a few sparse daily figures; no trend can be read from them. On the user's main concern, nothing new suggests other EU states are shifting migrants onto the Baltic states: the 2027 pool is still being negotiated, the Baltic states stand to receive priority support, and the only regular movement into a Baltic state from another EU country remains Estonia's lawful returns to Latvia of people who came via Belarus. That lawful practice is a knock-on effect of the Belarus route, not organised pressure. Finland's extended law and Estonia's coming road closure are security measures; a migrant push from Russia remains a contingency, not an observed movement.

headline: The European Court of Human Rights delivers its Grand Chamber rulings today on pushbacks at the Belarus border by Poland, Latvia and Lithuania. Russia formally protested Estonia's closure of its road crossings from 1 December. No new daily crossing figures and no plan to send migrants to the Baltic states from other EU countries.
pressure_note: No new official daily figures found after Latvia's 3 attempts on 18 November; Latvia's year total stays about 13,000 prevented attempts, with repeat attempts by the same people counted each time. Latvia's border guard says it has opened 179 criminal proceedings this year over moving people illegally across the border or enabling illegal stay. Pressure remains concentrated on Latvia.
eu_note: The Council has still not set the 2027 solidarity pool. Several outlets report that Latvia's interior minister asked the Commission to revise its 2027 assessment so that prevented crossing attempts count; we could not open these reports, so the details are unverified. Lithuania and Latvia remain listed as 'at risk', giving them priority access to EU support. No transfer or plan to send migrants to the Baltic states from western Europe was reported.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30 with no status or trend changes; 'Pushback law, courts and rights' stays Watch and Rising because the Grand Chamber rulings are due today, after this edition was written. All five counts stay at 0. New: Russia's foreign ministry protested Estonia's 1 December road-crossing closure; Latvian reports of a request to the Commission to revise its 2027 assessment. Clarification: Latvia's figure of 179 criminal proceedings this year covers both people smuggling and enabling illegal stay, which is why it is higher than the 138 smuggling cases in earlier editions.
bottom_line: Today's main event is the court ruling, not the border: the Grand Chamber judgments will say how far Poland, Latvia and Lithuania may turn people back at a border that Belarus uses for pressure, and both governments and rights groups will read them closely; we will report the findings tomorrow. Border pressure stays Elevated on Latvia's year total, which counts attempts rather than people, and the lack of new daily figures since 18 November is a publication gap, not evidence that crossings have stopped. On the user's main concern, nothing new suggests other EU states are shifting migrants onto the Baltic states: the 2027 pool is still undecided, and the reported Latvian request points the other way, toward lower obligations for Latvia. The only regular movement into a Baltic state from another EU country remains Estonia's lawful returns to Latvia of people who came via Belarus, a knock-on effect of the Belarus route rather than organised pressure. Russia's protest over Estonia's border closure raises political tension, but a migrant push from Russia remains a contingency, not an observed movement.

headline: The European Court of Human Rights ruled that sending people back to Belarus is not in itself unlawful when Minsk uses migration as a weapon, but found that Poland, Latvia and Lithuania each breached the rights of some applicants and ordered compensation. Latvia confirmed it has asked the Commission to treat it as under considerable migratory pressure. No plan to send migrants to the Baltic states from other EU countries.
pressure_note: No new official daily figures found after 18 November. Latvia's interior ministry gives 12,922 prevented attempts on the Belarus border this year up to 12 November, with repeat attempts by the same people counted each time; Lithuania has turned back nearly 2,000 people in 2026. A Belarusian exile outlet reported around 21 November that Latvia had its first two consecutive days without attempts since March; we could not read the full report. Pressure remains concentrated on Latvia.
eu_note: The Council has still not set the 2027 solidarity pool. Latvia's interior ministry confirmed it has asked the Commission to reassess it as under considerable migratory pressure, to count prevented crossings and instrumentalisation, and it is seeking exemption from its pool share. Nothing obliges a Baltic state to accept relocated people, and no transfer or plan to send migrants to the Baltic states from western Europe was reported.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30. 'Pushback law, courts and rights' stays Watch and its trend returns from Rising to Unchanged now that the judgments are out; 'Migration disinformation and rhetoric' stays Watch but its trend moves to Rising as oversimplified readings of the ruling spread. Counts: misleading migration claims rise from 0 to 1; the other four stay at 0. New: the Grand Chamber judgments of 24 November; reactions from Poland's government and Amnesty International; Latvia's request to the Commission, which earlier editions could not verify, is now confirmed by LSM.
bottom_line: The court's judgments are the main development and cut both ways: the Grand Chamber accepted that Belarus's use of migrants is a deliberate threat and that returning people there is not in itself inhuman treatment, but it required authorities to screen for children and other evidently vulnerable people and found violations in all three cases, including unlawful detention in Latvia and Lithuania and €15,000 for each Lithuanian applicant. Headlines run ahead of the text in both directions: 'pushbacks can be legal' leaves out the screening duty, and 'court clears Lithuania' leaves out the detention violations. Poland's government welcomed the ruling while Amnesty International called it a blow to the ban on torture; both readings contain part of the truth. On the user's main concern, nothing new suggests other EU states are shifting migrants onto the Baltic states: Latvia's confirmed request to the Commission seeks lower obligations, not more arrivals. Border pressure stays Elevated on Latvia's year total, which counts attempts rather than people, and the gap in daily figures is a publication gap, not proof that crossings have stopped.
